To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

health researchers who seek to increase the use and use of their research evidence in policy can work constructively with experienced newspaper journalists by: (1) appreciating journalists' roles, views and practices; and (2) cultivating relationships, synthesizing evidence, and communicating with journalists in ways that are consistent with their respective roles and that are relevant and accessible to readers.

health researchers should join the conversation by: (a) understanding journalists' roles, (b) respecting journalists' practices, (c) recognizing journalists' views, (d) appreciating journalists' contributions, (e) cultivating relationships, (f) communicating research evidence, and (g) participating in public conversations.

newspaper journalists' perspectives and suggestions for working with health researchers are important to know, because they can help health researchers increase research use in policymaking and improve health and healthcare.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how health researchers might engage with journalists as a way to promote the use of research in public policy making.
how health researchers can work constructively with the news media to improve health policy.
the question of how researchers can increase the use of their research evidence in public policy making.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
health researchers should work more closely with journalists, and that this would help to increase research use and improve health and healthcare.
health researchers can work with journalists by: (1) understanding journalists' roles and practices, (2) appreciating journalists' skepticism, and (3) cultivating relationships with journalists.

there are opportunities and benefits for policy-oriented health research and researchers to work constructurally with newspaper journalists, by appreciating their perspectives and by taking some of their suggestions seriously, and such engagement can be one means to increase the utilization of research evidence in the policy making process and thereby improve health.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
journalists want researchers to understand the role of the media in society, and that journalists are interested in researchers who are interested in them.
health researchers should work with journalists to improve public health and health care.
researchers and journalists can learn a lot from each other, if they take the time to do so.
The main takeaway from our work is that
health researchers should not assume that the media are a monolithic entity.

health researchers can work constructively with news media by understanding journalists' roles, processes and views, and by cultivating relationships with journalists as partners in public conversations about research evidence.
journalists and researchers are not adversaries but can work together to improve public health.
